explanation: The provisions for SCs are usually grouped under five heads: social, economic, educational and cultural, political, and service safeguards. Groupings differ between books (some use four or six heads), so this follows the official key.

exam: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
q:
Which of the following constitutional provisions provide reservation for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in India?

1. Article 15(4) & 15
(5) - Reservation in educational institutions.

2. Article 16(4) & 16(4A) - Reservation in government jobs.

3. Article 330 & 332 - Reservation in Parliament and State Legislatures.

4. Article 243D - Reservation in Panchayats.
5. Article 325 - Reservation in the Election Commission.
explanation:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (1, 2, 3 and 4 only); it is added as option 5.
Statements 1-4 are correct: 15(4)/15(5) education, 16(4)/16(4A) jobs, 330/332 legislatures and 243D panchayats; Art. 325 only bars exclusion from electoral rolls on religion, race, caste or sex – no reservation. No printed option has 1, 2, 3 and 4, so it is added ('1, 2 and 3 only' omits 243D).

notes.text: - **Art. 325** bars exclusion from electoral rolls on caste etc. – it gives **no reservation**.

q: Which of the following constitutional provisions is specifically designed to promote welfare for Scheduled Castes in India?
options: Article 15(4) - Special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes.
Article 46 - Promotion of welfare of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections.
Article 50 - Separation of judiciary from executive.

q: Which of the following policy measures is primarily aimed at improving the educational and economic status of Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in India?
options: Implementation of reservation in Parliament and State Assemblies.
Free education schemes and scholarships for SCs and STs.
Abolition of untouchability and social discrimination through the Right to Equality.
Establishment of special courts for the trial of crimes against SCs and STs.
key_text: Free education schemes and scholarships for SCs and STs.
explanation: Free education and scholarships directly improve the educational and economic status of SCs/STs; seat reservation is political, Art. 17 social, and special courts protective.

notes.text: - **Policy aimed at education + economy:** **free education and scholarships** (not seat reservation, Art. 17 or special courts).

q:
As per Article 164(1) of the Constitution of India, a minister in charge of tribal welfare who may in addition be in charge of the Scheduled Castes and backward classes is compulsory for which of the following states?

I. Madhya Pradesh

II. Punjab

III. Uttar Pradesh

IV. Jharkhand

V. Odisha
explanation: The proviso to Art. 164(1) (after the 94th Amendment, 2006) requires a tribal welfare minister in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha – so I, IV and V; Punjab and UP are not covered.

notes.text: - **Art. 164 proviso:** the **94th Amendment (2006)** replaced **Bihar** with Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand; Punjab and UP are not covered.

exam: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
q: How many seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Rajya Sabha?
explanation: No seats are reserved for SCs or STs in the Rajya Sabha; reservation (Arts 330, 332) is only in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.

notes.text: - Seats **in proportion to population**; **no separate electorate** – all voters of the constituency elect. **No SC/ST seats in the Rajya Sabha.**
